prompt_rules: Replace a complete URL, URI, or HTTP request target with one {variables}, including its scheme and path; do not retain internal prefixes.
Abstract every complete hostname:port or IP:port endpoint as one {variables} field wherever it appears; do not split the endpoint or partially preserve it.
Abstract a numeric port when its network role is explicit from a port field; do not treat every short integer as a port.
Abstract a complete hostname as {variables} when an explicit network field or phrase identifies it as a host, host.name, or node. Do not classify an arbitrary standalone word as a hostname.
Replace a complete filesystem path with one {variables}, including its leading or trailing slash, directory prefix, file name, and extension; do not retain internal path fragments.
Abstract a symbol-rich runtime identifier as one {variables} field when separators such as @, -, _, or dots are internal to the identifier rather than template punctuation.

Abstract a complete version number, including all numeric parts, as one {variables}. Preserve an attached product name and delimiter, as in Apache/{variables}. However, in a quoted HTTP request line, replace the complete protocol/version token, such as HTTP/1.1, with one {variables}. Preserve protocol names without a version, such as SOCKS5.
Abstract a process ID only when an explicit PID or process-ID field identifies it; preserve the surrounding key and punctuation.

Abstract task-attempt, task, job, stage, TID, and executor identifiers as {variables}. Preserve their role labels and delimiters. In scheduling messages, abstract the complete job name, including its namespace prefixes and suffixes.
Abstract an error or status code as {variables} when it appears in an explicit code or status field; preserve the surrounding event phrase.
Abstract an IRQ number as {variables} when it follows an IRQ label or interrupt-related phrase.

Abstract a device or network-interface identifier when it names the runtime object participating in an event, including values such as en0 or alt0. Preserve a device or interface name when it is part of fixed event wording; repeated occurrence alone does not make it fixed.

Preserve a class, module, method, protocol, service, or component name when it is part of fixed event wording. A fixed name remains fixed when it occurs inside parentheses; for example, preserve sshd in service(sshd) and preserve sshd:auth in pam_unix(sshd:auth).
Abstract a complete name when it is the value of an explicit name field, such as packageName.
Treat a process name appearing as the subject of a startup or shutdown event as a runtime process field and abstract it as {variables}.
Preserve a fixed range delimiter such as '-' or 'to' and replace its variable endpoints separately with {variables}.
Replace a packed numeric sequence or repeated numeric list with one {variables}.
In a key-value field, preserve a fixed key and the '=' or ':' delimiter and replace only its variable value with {variables}.
In an equality or comparison expression, preserve the operator and abstract only the variable operands.

Abstract an account identifier as {variables} when the context explicitly identifies a user or authentication identity. Abstract the account name after 'for' or 'user' in password or authentication messages, such as 'root' or 'admin'. Preserve the fixed status phrase 'user unknown', where unknown denotes authentication status rather than an account.
Abstract a state or boolean when it occupies a variable state or status field; preserve fixed action and event wording.
Abstract a flag or status value when it follows an explicit field name; preserve the field name, delimiter, and surrounding fixed text.

Never add, delete, move, or rewrite punctuation from the original log. Preserve brackets, parentheses, and quotation marks when they are fixed template syntax; include them in {variables} only when the complete wrapped text is one variable field.

Abstract data sizes and storage amounts as one {variables}, including number and unit. Preserve units in resource or hardware specifications and abstract only numbers. '47.8 GB' becomes '{variables}'. 'memory 2048 MB, disk 20 GB' becomes 'memory {variables} MB, disk {variables} GB'. Preserve bytes and punctuation.
A bracketed file:line marker immediately before an event is one source-location variable. Replace the entire text inside the brackets with one {variables}.

Preserve the following identifiers as literal template text in their stated roles: the software-agent name GoogleSoftwareUpdateAgent; the method name updateFinish; the protocol name SOCKS5; the fixed class or component name KSUpdateEngine; and the authentication-stage token preauth. Preserve main as a literal entry-point function name when it denotes the fixed function in the event template.
Preserve the device marker parport0 as literal template text in the observed event family.

Preserve the fixed event phrase "Out of memory" as literal template text. Preserve the fixed phrase "Bye Bye" as literal template text. Preserve the fixed event outcome phrase "disconnected by user" as literal template text.
Preserve the key token lvl in a field such as [lvl={variables}]; abstract only its value.
Preserve GET as a fixed HTTP method token.
